summary: The main risks are API completeness, update-time convention lookup, context/precedence ambiguity, and enforcing limits consistently across all write paths. The existing TemplateEngine can support this, but JiraToolkit needs a dedicated resolver and stronger error/test contracts.

suggestions.title: Centralize rendering and template selection
suggestions.rationale: The three write methods independently build payloads, while create resolves defaults and canonical issue types before constructing `issue_fields`. Add one private Jira-specific rendering helper and call it after those resolutions so selection, context merging, escaping, and length guarding cannot diverge across create, update, and comment paths.

suggestions.title: Permit template-only comments
suggestions.rationale: `jira_add_comment` and `AddCommentInput` currently require `body: str`. A caller cannot use a comment template without supplying a redundant body, so the tool contract should make `body` optional and reject only when both body and template are absent.

suggestions.title: Define update fallback metadata resolution
suggestions.rationale: The update path receives only an issue key plus optional update fields, but convention lookup needs project and issue type. The current implementation fetches the issue inside the blocking `_run` function immediately before update, too late for an async template render. Specify whether update auto-selection performs a metadata fetch first, renders only with an explicit template, or renders within a redesigned transport boundary.

suggestions.title: Make template names canonical and listable
suggestions.rationale: `TemplateEngine` resolves raw loader names and exposes no listing operation, while the agent-facing contract requires `jira_list_templates`. Define whether `template='bug'` maps to `bug.j2`, return deterministic logical names such as `NAV/bug`, normalize case consistently, and prevent absolute or traversal names. Listing should expose names, not filesystem paths or source.

suggestions.title: Freeze the template context shape before implementation
suggestions.rationale: Create currently transforms project, issue type, assignee, and components before sending the final fields, whereas update and comment expose different inputs. The phrase “call fields merged with template_params” must specify field names, nesting, and whether resolved account IDs/components are present. Compute convention selection from resolved call values before applying the documented params-win overlay, and pass only serializable data rather than Jira objects.

suggestions.title: Resolve conflicts with arbitrary fields explicitly
suggestions.rationale: Both create and update merge `fields` after setting standard fields. Therefore `fields={'description': ...}` can silently replace a rendered description, making an explicit template ineffective. Reject duplicate description keys when templating, or document and test a single authoritative precedence rule.

suggestions.title: Make length guarding centralized and field-specific
suggestions.rationale: `ResearchNode` already summarizes and truncates descriptions to 30,000 characters, while JiraToolkit currently forwards descriptions and comments without a shared guard. A template can add enough wrapper text to overflow after ResearchNode finishes. Guard the final rendered value in the toolkit, count the marker within the limit, define separate policies for descriptions and comments, and test the double-guard path.

suggestions.title: Handle missing template directories without hiding configuration errors
suggestions.rationale: `TemplateEngine.__init__` raises `ValueError` for a nonexistent directory. JiraToolkit construction must remain usable with only in-memory templates or no templates, so initialization must be lazy or omit nonexistent directories. Still emit a clear warning for an explicitly configured missing path so a typo in `JIRA_TEMPLATES_DIR` is diagnosable.

suggestions.title: Provide aggregate missing-variable diagnostics
suggestions.rationale: The engine uses `StrictUndefined`, but `TemplateEngine.render` wraps the first Jinja template error into a generic `ValueError`. That does not guarantee the U3 contract of naming all missing variables. Add a Jira-specific error containing the template name and missing names, ensure no Jira transport occurs, and distinguish missing templates from render failures.

suggestions.title: Expand the frozen-surface tests into a rendering matrix
suggestions.rationale: The current tests freeze constructor/tool signatures and only assert that write methods still reference `self.jira`. Add tests for byte-for-byte no-template behavior, disabled autoescape, in-memory-over-filesystem precedence, explicit versus convention selection, lowercase `.j2` names, params-win context merging, template-only comments, empty rendered descriptions, missing-variable transport suppression, update metadata lookup, field conflicts, and final truncation.
